question: I invested money in a trading app after seeing it promoted on WhatsApp, but now I can't withdraw my money. What should I do?
reference_answer: The app initially shows fake profits to lure victims into investing more, but later blocks withdrawals and demands fees or excuses. You should stop all further investment and report the incident to the cybercrime helpline.

steps.text: Stop all further payments to the app or any person claiming to help you withdraw funds. Do not take loans or transfer more money to 'unlock' your account.
Realise that the app is likely a fake trading platform: profits shown are fake, and withdrawal is blocked with excuses or fees (see passage sebi-f7196f25#0004, steps 3‑6).
Contact your bank immediately and request to stop or reverse the UPI/digital payment transaction. Ask the bank to block the beneficiary account.
Report the fraud on the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (cybercrime.gov.in) or call the dedicated helpline 1930 for immediate assistance.
File a written complaint with your local cyber cell / police, providing all chat screenshots, transaction IDs, and the app name/URL.
Warn friends or family who might see the same WhatsApp/Telegram ads: the scam uses attractive ads, fake 'expert' tips, and fake profit screenshots to lure victims (sebi-f7196f25#0004).

question: I got a call from someone saying they're from the Reserve Bank of India, asking for my debit card PIN and the three-digit code on the back. Is this a real RBI call?
reference_answer: The Reserve Bank of India does not call or email people asking for debit card PINs or CVV numbers, and no legitimate bank requests such details over the phone or via email.

steps.text: Report the financial fraud immediately on the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (www.cybercrime.gov.in) or call the helpline 1930 for prompt assistance.
If you have already shared bank account or card details, inform your bank so they can monitor or secure your account.
Do not share any bank account, PIN, CVV, or OTP details with unknown callers or via email, as RBI has warned against phishing mails/calls seeking such details.
Report suspected fraud communications (e.g., suspicious calls, SMS, WhatsApp) through the Sanchar Saathi portal to help telecom authorities take action.

reference_answer: If you received a suspected fraud communication, report it on the Chakshu platform of the Department of Telecommunications at sancharsaathi.gov.in/sfc/ within 30 days. If you have already lost money, report the cybercrime at the helpline number 1930 or website cybercrime.gov.in.

reference_answer: Do not click the link, as it may be fraudulent and could lead to money loss. The public is advised not to fall prey to frauds being perpetrated in the name of KYC updation.

steps.text: Do not click the link or share any OTP/account details; this is a known KYC‑updation fraud modus operandi.

Always access your bank’s official website or contact your branch directly to verify KYC status.
If you have already lost money, report immediately to the 1930 helpline or cybercrime.gov.in.

question: I got a call from someone claiming to be from the RBI or a government agency, saying my bank account will be blocked unless I share my OTP and install a given app. Is this real?
reference_answer: The RBI has warned that fraudsters impersonate officials and threaten to freeze or block bank accounts, then ask victims to share OTP, PIN, or install unverified applications. Such calls are scams and should be ignored.

steps.text: Immediately end the call. Do not share your OTP, do not download any app, and do not provide any bank details. Official advisories state that RBI does not send such calls, nor does it ask individuals to deposit money or share OTPs for account protection.
If you have already shared any details or installed the app, disconnect the call right away and do not follow any further instructions from the caller.
Report the incident through the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal at cybercrime.gov.in or call the dedicated helpline 1930 for immediate assistance.
Contact your bank’s official customer-care number (found on the back of your card or the bank’s website) to inform them of the attempted fraud and to secure your account.
Do not trust Caller-ID displays; cybercriminals can spoof names such as "RBI" or "Government agency". RBI has warned that such calls claiming account-blockage are fraudulent.
Never share your UPI PIN, OTP, or install any screen‑sharing or remote‑access app at the request of an unknown caller, even if they claim to be from a regulatory authority.
Save any call‑record, message, or app‑installation evidence and provide it when filing the cyber‑crime complaint; this aids investigation and potential recovery.

draft.text: Immediately end the call. Do not share your OTP, do not download any app, and do not provide any bank details. Official advisories state that RBI does not send such calls, nor does it ask individuals to deposit money or share OTPs for account protection.
If you have already shared any details or installed the app, disconnect the call right away and do not follow any further instructions from the caller.
Report the incident through the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal at cybercrime.gov.in or call the dedicated helpline 1930 for immediate assistance.
Contact your bank’s official customer-care number (found on the back of your card or the bank’s website) to inform them of the attempted fraud and to secure your account.
Do not trust Caller-ID displays; cybercriminals can spoof names such as "RBI" or "Government agency". RBI has warned that such calls claiming account-blockage are fraudulent.
Never share your UPI PIN, OTP, or install any screen‑sharing or remote‑access app at the request of an unknown caller, even if they claim to be from a regulatory authority.
Save any call‑record, message, or app‑installation evidence and provide it when filing the cyber‑crime complaint; this aids investigation and potential recovery.

question: व्हाट्सएप या टेलीग्राम पर कोई ट्रेडिंग ऐप दिखे, जो जल्दी ज्यादा मुनाफा देने का वादा करे, क्या वो भरोसेमंद होता है?
reference_answer: The passage warns that scammers lure investors with promises of high returns through fake trading apps and social media groups, indicating such offers are typically untrustworthy.

steps.text: नहीं, ऐसे ऐप भरोसेमंद नहीं होते। SEBI के अनुसार, ट्रेडिंग ऐप से जुड़े विज्ञापन या सुझाव जो जल्दी ज्यादा मुनाफा देने का वादा करते हैं, अक्सर फ्रॉड होते हैं। SEBI ने चेतावनी दी है कि सोशल मीडिया पर ऐसे ऐप का प्रचार करने वाले "विशेषज्ञ" असली नहीं होते और ऐप्स गैरकानूनी तरीके से पैसे जमा करवाते हैं।
ऐसे ऐप से दूर रहें और किसी भी तरह का निवेश न करें। SEBI ने साफ किया है कि गारंटीड रिटर्न का वादा करना प्रतिभूति बाजार में एक घोटाला है।
यदि आपने पहले ही कोई ऐप डाउनलोड कर लिया है या पैसा ट्रांसफर कर दिया है, तो तुरंत साइबर क्राइम हेल्पलाइन 1930 पर शिकायत दर्ज कराएं या cybercrime.gov.in पर जाएं।
अपने बैंक को सूचित करें और उस ऐप से जुड़े किसी भी तीसरे पक्ष के खाते में भेजे गए पैसे के बारे में बताएं ताकि बैंक तुरंत कार्रवाई कर सके।
भविष्य में हमेशा SEBI के पंजीकृत ट्रेडिंग ऐप्स की जांच करें। SEBI के निवेशक पोर्टल पर जाएं और "Registered Mobile Trading Apps" सेक्शन में ऐप का नाम सर्च करें।

The step correctly paraphrases the cited passage's statement that 'Unrealistic promises (guaranteed returns in the securities market are a scam!)'. The step's assertion that SEBI clarified guaranteed returns are a scam is directly supported.

The step accurately reflects the cited passage's instruction to 'Report any suspicious activity to cyber cell, I4C helpline 1930' and the provided link to cybercrime.gov.in. The passage explicitly provides these contact details for victims who have already engaged with such apps.

The step is supported by the cited passage, which explicitly advises 'Avoid transferring money to personal accounts; always use the official app or website of a registered broker' and warns about scammers imposing hidden fees when victims withdraw funds, hindering recovery.

The step directly mirrors the cited passage's instruction to 'Verify platform legitimacy (check on Exchanges website or SEBI Investor website under Registered Mobile Trading Apps Section)' and the action of searching the 'Registered Mobile Trading Apps' section on the SEBI Investor portal.
